text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Limited cabinet reshuffle within hours to be followed by movements among governors. Six ministers to be changed in bid to answer requirements of economic takeoff by adding new blood.
- Ehud Barak accuses Netanyahu of dragging Israel towards war.
- Private sector to contribute 81 percent of investments in industry in new five year plan.
- 700,000 new telephones and 200 million pounds for road improvement.
- In a message to Kuwaiti emir, Mubarak says Egypt wants to boost relations with Kuwait.
- Ministerial committee for tourism development to discuss 155 new projects worth 7.6 billion pounds.
- Military prosecutors reveal that women of Gama'a al-Islamiya used to carry orders and explosives and used to shelter terrorists.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says Egypt is battling attempts to kill peace.
- Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says in France that Egyptian satellite will be launched in January.
- Archaeologists find Coptic city in Isna desert.
- Head of port security says no mad cow meat in Egypt.
